参议员罗杰·威克表示，他希望特朗普就“中国大规模扩军的目的，以及中国对伊朗的明显支持”向习近平施压。 On Tuesday, Senator Roger Wicker, Republican of Mississippi and chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, said in a speech on the Senate floor that he would have advised against the invitation to the “brutal, unelected and oppressive dictator who seeks to dominate his neighbors and whose massive military arsenal is aimed directly at the United States of America.” 周二，密西西比州共和党参议员、参议院军事委员会主席罗杰·威克 在参议院发表讲话 说，如果征求他的意见，他会 建议不要邀请 这位“残暴、未经选举产生、实行压迫统治的独裁者；此人企图称霸邻国，其庞大的军事武库直接瞄准美利坚合众国”。 Mr. Wicker said he hoped Mr. Trump would press Mr. Xi on “the purposes of China’s massive military buildup, or about China’s clear support for Iran.” 威克说，他希望特朗普就“中国大规模扩军的目的，以及中国对伊朗的明显支持”向习近平施压。 Responding to Mr. Wicker’s comments, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the visit reflected an acknowledgment by Mr. Trump that despite disagreements, China is one of the largest economic and military powers in the world. 针对威克的言论，国务卿鲁比奥回应称，此次访问体现出特朗普认识到，尽管双方存在分歧，中国仍是世界上最大的经济与军事力量之一。 “The relationship between the United States and China will define the 21st century, what happens in that relationship,” Mr. Rubio said. “The idea that we would not interact with them at the highest levels is irresponsible. It’s outrageous. We have to.” “美中关系将定义21世纪，美中关系将决定21世纪，决定这个世纪会发生什么，”鲁比奥说，“认为我们不应在最高层级上与他们互动，这种想法是不负责任的，是荒谬的。我们必须这样做。” Foreign policy experts say that Mr. Trump’s posture has been striking even for a president who prides himself on his personal brand of diplomacy. 外交政策专家表示，即便对于一位以个人外交为傲的总统来说，特朗普的姿态也格外引人注目。 “Trump is displaying an extraordinary degree of deference to Xi,” said Julian Gewirtz, a scholar at Columbia University who has written on the history of U.S.-China relations. “He is lavishing honors on China’s leader while downplaying threats to American interests. Beijing could scarcely have asked for a more accommodating host.” “特朗普对习近平表现出了非同寻常的顺从，”研究美中关系史的哥伦比亚大学学者朱利安·格维茨说。“他给予中国领导人极高礼遇，同时淡化对美国利益的威胁。北京方面几乎不可能遇到一个更迁就自己的东道主了。” Mr. Gewirtz, who also served a former White House and State Department official working on China under President Joseph R. Biden Jr., said that traditionally it has been Beijing that has sought out a state visit. This time, he said, the dynamic seems reversed. What Mr. Trump emerges with from all of the spectacle will be a test of his brand of diplomacy, which emphasizes personal ties. 格维茨曾在拜登总统任内担任白宫和国务院负责中国事务的官员。他说，过去通常是北京方面寻求进行国事访问，而这一次，双方的态势似乎反了过来。特朗普从这一系列引人注目的场面中究竟能收获什么，将是对他那套强调私人关系的外交风格的考验。 “Washington has often leveraged symbolic honors to seek substantive gains from Beijing,” he said. “So the question is straightforward: What is Trump getting for America in return for all this ceremony?” “华盛顿过去常常利用象征性的礼遇，来换取北京方面在实质问题上的让步，”他说。“所以问题很简单：特朗普用这一整套隆重礼遇究竟为美国换来了什么？” In a call with reporters, White House officials said the agenda with Mr. Xi will include topics like artificial intelligence, fentanyl and the upcoming expiration of a trade truce. 在与记者的电话吹风会上，白宫官员表示，此次与习近平的会谈议程将涉及人工智能、芬太尼以及即将到期的贸易休战协议等议题。 Asked whether the president planned to raise Mr. Trump’s allegations that China interfered in the 2020 election, the White House had no comment. 当被问及总统是否打算提出他此前关于中国干预2020年大选的指控时，白宫没有发表评论。 一名要求匿名的白宫官员指出，美国已采取多项措施对中国经济造成了影响，包括对美出口显著下降。 Another White House official pushed back against the premise that Mr. Trump was overly deferential to Mr. Xi. The official pointed to a number of measures the United States has taken that have affected China’s economy , including a marked decline on exports to the United States. 另一名白宫官员则反驳了特朗普对习近平过于迁就的说法。这名官员列举了美国采取的多项 影响中国经济 的措施，其中包括中国对美出口的明显下降。 The person said the United States has targeted some entities that have been found to support Iran — though no major banks — and that other measures are in the works behind the scenes that have not yet been announced. 这名官员说，美国已对部分被查实支持伊朗的实体实施了制裁——不过其中没有大型银行——此外还有其他措施正在幕后推进，尚未公布。 The officials spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the visit ahead of time. 由于是在访问开始前讨论相关情况，这些官员均要求匿名。 (Last month, when Mr. Trump was asked why he was not targeting Chinese banks the way he was generally targeting allies like Canada, he snapped back: “Well, who said I’m not? You said, why not. I mean, who said I’m not. You don’t know if I’m doing it. Well, I don’t have to announce everything, do I?”) （上个月，当特朗普被问到为什么没有像通常针对加拿大等盟友那样针对中国的银行时，他厉声反驳道：“谁说我没有？你问为什么没有。我的意思是，谁说我没有？你又不知道我有没有这么做。我没必要什么事都公之于众，对吧？”） A Treasury Department spokesman said in a follow-up email that Secretary Scott Bessent, who is spearheading the so-called “Operation Economic Outcast” operation, has made it clear to China that it will not hesitate to hold them accountable for supporting Iran economically. 财政部一名发言人随后在电子邮件中表示，牵头 所谓“经济放逐行动” 的财政部长斯科特·贝森特已经向中国明确表示，对于中国在经济上支持伊朗，美国会毫不犹豫地追究其责任。 In recent weeks, when pressed about China’s behavior, Mr. Trump at several points seemed to make excuses for Mr. Xi. 最近几周，当被追问中国的行为时，特朗普有好几次似乎都在替习近平开脱。 During an Oval Office event this month in which he called the war in Iran “small potatoes,” Mr. Trump suggested that China’s aid to Iran was negligible because of his personal plea. 本月在白宫椭圆形办公室的一场活动上，特朗普称伊朗战争是“小事一桩”，并暗示由于他亲自出面提出了请求，中国对伊朗的援助微不足道。 “I said, please don’t get involved to President Xi — I have a very good relationship,” Mr. Trump said. “And they’re not really involved. Very little involvement by China. China could have plenty of involvement. They get 50 percent of the oil from the Hormuz strait.” “我对习近平主席说，请不要介入——我和他关系非常好，”特朗普说。“他们实际上没有怎么介入。中国介入得非常少。中国本来可以大举介入。他们有50%的石油要经过霍尔木兹海峡。” 中国没有表现出任何要减少与伊朗商业往来的迹象，公然无视美国在全球范围内切断德黑兰经济命脉的行动。 Later in the month, when asked about reports that Chinese entities may have provided the Iranians with satellite imagery that led to deadly strikes on U.S. forces in Jordan, again Mr. Trump demurred . 当月晚些时候，当被问及有关中国实体可能向伊朗提供卫星图像、帮助伊朗发动造成驻约旦美军死亡的袭击的报道时， 特朗普再次避而不答 。 “They basically do what we do,” he said. “基本上他们做的和我们一样，”他说。 “Are you going to raise that with Xi when he visits?” a reporter asked. “习近平来访时，你会向他提出这件事吗？”一名记者问。 “I think he’s behaved reasonably well, and we behave reasonably well,” Mr. Trump said. “You know when they say that China spies on us, I say you’re right, and we spy on them too. You know, we spy on them too.” “我认为他的表现还算不错，我们的表现也还算不错，”特朗普说。“你知道，当他们说中国刺探我们的情报时，我会说，你说得对，我们也刺探他们的情报。你知道，我们也刺探他们的情报。” Pressed during a Fox News interview about what Mr. Xi may want from his visit, Mr. Trump pivoted to his consistent refrain: “You know, he and I get along very well.” 在接受福克斯新闻采访、被问及习近平可能希望从此次访问中得到什么时，特朗普再次搬出了他一贯的说辞：“你知道，他和我处得非常好。” That the visit comes after Mr. Trump has spent weeks escalating attacks on America’s allies presents a particularly jarring split-screen, several foreign policy analysts say. 多名外交政策分析人士指出，这次访问恰逢特朗普连续数周 不断升级对美国盟友的攻击言论 之际，两相对照，形成了尤其强烈的反差。 “There’s a rule of international politics that American presidents normally follow: treat your allies better than your adversaries,” said R. Nicholas Burns, the top U.S. diplomat in Beijing under the Biden administration. “And we don’t want to give the impression to our allies that we actually care more about this relationship with Xi Jinping than we care about the relationship with them. I think the president is giving that impression by being so unremittingly uncritical of the Chinese.” “国际政治有一条美国历任总统通常都会遵循的规则：对盟友的态度理应好于对对手的态度，”拜登政府时期的美国驻华大使尼古拉斯·伯恩斯说。“我们不希望让盟友产生这样的印象：相比与他们的关系，我们其实更重视与习近平的关系。我认为，总统对中国如此不加批评正在给人造成这种印象。” Mr. Burns added that Mr. Trump’s tactics are unlikely to work on China, which he said responds to strength. 伯恩斯还说，特朗普的这套策略不太可能在中国身上奏效，因为在他看来，中国只会对实力做出回应。 “They are practical, hardheaded, cynical about the United States,” Mr. Burns said. “They’re going to judge us, I think, by how strong we are and how much we push back when we have to push back. I think the Chinese understand power and deterrence. They’ll be swayed more and affected more by a strong American position than they will by flattery.” “他们务实、强硬，对美国抱有怀疑，”伯恩斯说。“我认为，他们会根据我们有多强大以及在必要时的反击力度来判断我们。我认为中国人理解实力和威慑。相比奉承，美国采取强硬立场更能影响到他们。” If previous summits are any indication, Mr. Trump’s pageantry and flattery to impress Mr. Xi won’t go far, analysts say. When the two met in Korea last year to de-escalate a fierce trade war , for example, Mr. Trump did most of the talking and Mr. Xi stayed largely silent. Mr. Trump called Mr. Xi “a friend of mine” and called him “powerful.” The Chinese president approached the meeting with caution and steeliness. In his remarks, Mr. Xi likened China-U.S. relations to a “giant ship” that requires steady joint leadership. 分析人士说，如果以过去的峰会为参照，特朗普试图以盛大排场和奉承给习近平留下深刻印象，不会产生多大作用。例如， 两人去年在韩国会晤、试图缓和激烈的贸易战时 ，大部分时间都是特朗普在讲话，习近平基本保持沉默。特朗普称习近平是“我的朋友”，还说他是“强有力的领导人”。习近平则以谨慎而强硬的态度参加会晤。在讲话中，他把中美关系比作一艘需要双方稳健共同掌舵的“大船”。 The two leaders come to the U.S. summit in vastly different positions, said Jonathan A. Czin, a researcher at the Brookings Institution who previously worked at the C.I.A. analyzing Chinese politics. 曾在中央情报局从事中国政治分析工作、现为布鲁金斯学会研究员的秦江南(Jonathan A. Czin)表示，两位领导人此次在美国举行峰会所处的形势可谓截然不同。 Mr. Xi arrives with time on his side , hoping to buy more for relief from U.S. pressure, as he plans for a fourth term that will keep him in power for another five years. Mr. Trump is facing a midterm election in a few weeks in which his party has an uphill battle as a result of some of his policies. 习近平 占据时间上的优势 ，他希望借此为自己争取更多喘息空间，以缓解来自美方的压力——毕竟他正在为即将到来的第四个任期做准备，这将使他继续执掌大权五年之久。特朗普则将在几周后面临中期选举，由于他的一些政策，其所在政党面临一场艰难的选战。 “Xi is going to walk into this meeting and is going to be keenly aware of the fact that just weeks from now, Trump is in all likelihood going to be at best a lame-duck president, and at worst, he’s going to be politically maimed at home and have to deal with divided government,” Mr. Czin said. “习近平走进这场会晤时，会非常清楚地意识到一个事实：再过几个星期，特朗普很可能最好的结果是成为一名跛脚鸭总统；最坏的情况下，他在国内政治上将遭受重创，还不得不面对一个分裂的政府，” 秦江南说。 He continued: “Xi is already thinking about ‘How am I going to keep this gentlemen’s agreement going with the United States,’ buying that time, and already thinking about what comes after Trump.” 他接着说：“习近平已经在思考，‘我怎样才能让与美国达成的这项君子协定继续维持下去’，从而争取时间；而且他已经在考虑特朗普卸任之后的局面该如何应对。” Mr. Trump has long had an affinity for autocrats. He regularly boasts about his relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin. This summer he trumpeted what he said was his good relationship with North Korea’s dictator, Kim Jong-un, while canceling long-running military exercise s with South Korea, a U.S. ally. 特朗普向来对威权领导人抱有好感。他时常炫耀自己与俄罗斯总统普京的关系。今年夏天,他还大肆宣扬自己与朝鲜独裁者金正恩之间所谓的良好关系。同时却 取消了与美国盟友韩国之间由来已久的联合军事演习 。 Ruth Ben-Ghiat, a historian at New York University who studies fascism and authoritarianism, said that Mr. Trump has always admired Mr. Xi as having the kind of power he covets. 纽约大学研究法西斯主义与威权主义的历史学家露丝·本-吉亚特表示，特朗普一直以来都很欣赏习近平，因为后者拥有他所渴求的那种权力。 She pointed out that Mr. Trump’s doomsday declaration last month that “communism is the greatest threat to our country in its history,” had no bearing on Mr. Trump’s “fawning” over the leader of one of the powerful communist countries. 她指出，特朗普上个月曾发出末日般的警告，称“共产主义是我国历史上面临的最大威胁”，但这丝毫没有影响特朗普对一个强大共产党国家领导人的“奉承讨好”。 She also pointed to Mr. Trump’s latest defense of China’s government last week when a reporter raised that it was one of the most repressive countries in the world for journalists. Mr. Trump interrupted the reporter’s question, responding: “Well, I don’t know about that. I think we’re repressive also.” (That same day he would ban news organizations whose coverage he doesn’t like from the White House grounds). 她还提到，上周有记者提出中国是全球对新闻记者压制最为严厉的国家之一时，特朗普再度为中国政府进行了辩护。特朗普打断了那名记者的提问，回应道：“这个嘛，我倒不这么认为。我觉得我们自己也挺压制的。”（就在同一天，他宣布禁止他不满其报道内容的新闻机构进入白宫区域。） “This meeting of head of states has importance for the optics it generates,” Ms. Ben-Ghiat said. “Two powerful strongmen, meeting as equals, at least in Trump’s mind — and for the potential for deals conducted in a nontransparent fashion.” 本-吉亚特说，“这次国家元首会晤的重要性在于它所制造出的视觉效果——两位强大的铁腕人物以对等身份会面，至少在特朗普看来是如此。此外还在于以不透明方式达成交易的可能性。” Erica L. Green 是时报白宫记者，报道特朗普总统及其政府。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 中美AI竞赛：美国在哪些领域领先、哪些领域落后？
description: DUSTIN VOLZ, CADE METZ2026年9月24日7月在上海举行的世界人工智能大会。中美两国正陷入一场人工智能竞赛，双方都认为这场竞赛对在军事、技术和经济领域占据上风至关重要。 Ng Han Guan/Associated Press There is no shortage of issues on the table for possible discussion as President Trump prepares to welcome the Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, for a state visit beginning Wednesday evening, including the Iran war, Taiwan and tariffs. 特朗普总统将在周三晚间起迎接中国国家主席习近平进行国事访问，届时将有很多问题需要讨论，包括伊朗战争、台湾和关税问题。 But no topic has captured global fascination in recent weeks more than whether the two sides can reach any agreements around the pace of artificial intelligence development. The rapidly shifting debate about the risks of A.I. has so consumed Silicon Valley, Washington and, in recent days, the United Nations that some observers have likened the U.S.-China summit to a Cold War tête-à-tête during the nuclear arms race. 但在最近几周，没有任何话题比双方能否就人工智能的发展速度达成共识更令全球关注。关于人工智能风险快速变化的辩论已彻底席卷硅谷和华盛顿，近日波及联合国，以至于一些观察家将此次美中峰会比作核军备竞赛期间的冷战一对一会谈。 Though some see the stakes this week as nothing short of civilizational, the expectations for any serious accord remain low. The countries are locked in an A.I. race that both sides see as decisive to gaining the upper hand militarily, technologically and economically, and mutual suspicion runs deep, according to foreign policy analysts. 尽管有人认为本周的博弈事关文明存亡，但人们对达成任何实质性协议的期望依然很低。外交政策分析人士表示，两国正陷入人工智能竞赛，双方都认为这场竞赛将决定谁能在军事、技术和经济上占据上风，而且双方的相互猜疑根深蒂固。 Western experts generally estimate that the United States is somewhere around six months ahead of China in the A.I. race when it comes to its leading models. But that figure obscures the complex relationship between the two nations, further complicating efforts to reach agreement on how to address A.I. safety risks. 西方专家普遍估计，在人工智能竞赛中，就领先模型而言，美国领先中国约六个月左右。但这个数字掩盖了两国之间复杂的关系，进一步增加了就应对人工智能安全风险达成共识的难度。 Here is a look at where the United States has the upper hand against China on A.I. and where it is lagging behind its top geopolitical rival. 以下是美国在人工智能领域相对于中国的优势所在，以及落后于其头号地缘政治对手的领域。 历届美国政府都实施了出口管制措施，限制了中国获得高性能芯片的渠道，其中包括英伟达生产的芯片。 Access to top-shelf computer chips is paramount. 获取顶级计算机芯片至关重要。 The United States has one undeniable advantage over China: computer chips. Most of the specialized chips used to build and operate A.I. technologies are designed by American companies. This includes the Silicon Valley chipmaker Nvidia, which is now the world’s most valuable company. 相对于中国，美国有一个不可否认的优势：计算机芯片。用于构建和运行人工智能技术的大多数专用芯片都是由美国公司设计的，其中包括现在全球市值最高的公司——硅谷芯片制造商英伟达。 “The people who have made the fastest chips are here,” said Andrew Feldman, the chief executive of the Silicon Valley chipmaker Cerebras. “And they are not in China.” “制造出最快芯片的人在这里，”硅谷芯片制造商Cerebras的首席执行官安德鲁·费尔德曼说。“他们不在中国。” Over the past decade, three American presidential administrations have imposed export controls that limited Chinese access to powerful chips. Even as China works to evade these controls, Chinese A.I. researchers often say that chip shortages are the biggest obstacle they face. 过去十年里，三届美国政府都实施了出口管制，限制中国获取强大的芯片。尽管中国努力规避这些管制，但中国的人工智能研究人员经常表示，芯片短缺是他们面临的最大障碍。 The leading Chinese companies have spent hundreds of millions of dollars to secure the chips they need. To bypass American export controls, they often buy remote access to data centers outside of China. Over the past year, this allowed China to shrink the performance gap between its systems and the leading American technologies. 中国领先企业已经花费数亿美元来获取所需芯片。为了绕过美国的出口管制，他们经常购买对中国境外数据中心的远程访问权限。过去一年里，这使得中国缩小了其系统与美国领先技术之间的性能差距。 At the same time, China is working to build its own chip-making industry. But by its own admission, Huawei, the telecommunications and electronics company that leads this effort, is still years away from producing chips that perform as well as those offered by Nvidia today. 与此同时，中国正在努力建立自己的芯片制造产业。但引领这一努力的电信和电子公司华为也承认，距离生产出性能可与英伟达当前产品媲美的芯片仍需数年时间。 Chinese A.I. companies say they are already using chips from Huawei, but these chips are unlikely to provide much help in building cutting-edge technologies. Less-powerful chips are typically used to serve technologies to users across the internet. 中国人工智能公司表示，他们已经在使用华为的芯片，但这些芯片不太可能为构建尖端技术提供太多帮助。性能较弱的芯片通常用于通过互联网向用户提供技术服务。 Even with help from Huawei, Chinese A.I. companies like Moonshot have struggled to find the additional chips they need to meet demand. 即使有华为的帮助，像月之暗面这样的中国人工智能公司仍难以找到满足需求的额外芯片。 As Americans sour on A.I., China faces fewer headwinds politically. 美国人对人工智能日益感到反感，中国在政治上面临的阻力较小。 Public polling in the United States shows that A.I. has become increasingly unpopular over the past year — so much so that it has now become a key issue in the midterm elections. Many Americans are worried about A.I. threatening their jobs, undermining education and, more recently, posing a threat to humanity. A Pew Research Center poll this week found that 60 percent of Americans were uncomfortable with a new local data center. 美国的民意调查显示，人工智能在过去一年里变得越来越不受欢迎——以至于它现在已成为中期选举的一个关键议题。许多美国人担心人工智能会威胁他们的工作、破坏教育，而最近更担心它会对人类构成威胁。皮尤研究中心本周的一项民调发现，60%的美国人对新建本地数据中心感到不安。 Though Mr. Trump has dismissed calls for an A.I. slowdown as a “hoax,” a growing number of Republican and Democratic lawmakers, governors and 2028 presidential hopefuls are scrambling to offer a wide range of proposals seeking to regulate the technology after disclosures about rogue A.I. agents hacking into other companies. 尽管特朗普将放缓人工智能发展的呼吁斥为“骗局”，但在有关失控的人工智能智能体黑客入侵其他公司的事件曝光后，越来越多的共和党及民主党议员、州长以及2028年总统大选的有望参选者，正争先恐后地提出各种提案，试图对这项技术进行监管。 By nature of its centralized systems, China does not need to contend with a boisterous public debate about how or whether to rein in A.I. And though polling in China can be dubious, surveys consistently point to more enthusiasm for its adoption. 由于中国实行集中式管理体制，因此无需面对是否以及如何限制人工智能的激烈公众辩论。而且，尽管中国的民意调查可能值得怀疑，但各项调查始终显示，公众对采用人工智能的态度更为积极。 Chinese citizens broadly appear to be much more optimistic about A.I. — and in fact are some of the most hopeful about the technology in the entire world, according to a KPMG survey of 47 countries last year. Some 69 percent of people in China said the technology’s benefits outweighed its risks, compared with just 35 percent of Americans who agreed. The technology is also more embedded in day-to-day life, including service robots in hotels and restaurants, as well as medical chatbots at hospitals. 中国公民似乎普遍对人工智能要乐观得多——事实上，根据毕马威去年对47个国家进行的一项调查，他们是全世界对该技术抱有最大希望的人群之一。约69%的中国人表示，这项技术的好处大于风险，相比之下，持相同观点的美国人仅占35%。这项技术也更多地融入了日常生活，包括酒店和餐厅的服务机器人，以及医院的医疗聊天机器人。 The U.S. economy has so far been more resilient to huge investments in A.I. 到目前为止，美国经济在面对人工智能领域的巨额投资时表现出了更强的韧性。 Another advantage for the United States is that its economy has been more resilient during the A.I. boom. Stock indexes are near record highs, and worries of an A.I. bubble also have so far not materialized. Fears of job losses prompted by the technology proliferating throughout corporate America have yet to really appear in economic data. 美国的另一个优势是，在人工智能热潮期间，其经济更具韧性。股票指数接近历史高点，对人工智能泡沫的担忧迄今也未成为现实。尽管这项技术正在美国企业界广泛普及，但由此引发的失业担忧尚未在经济数据中真正显现。 There are some signs that A.I. is contributing to slower wage growth in jobs most exposed to the technology and fewer job openings, especially for young workers. And applying to jobs, especially for entry-level workers, has become even more daunting thanks to A.I. being used to either write résumés or screen applicants. But overall, the economic distress directly linked to A.I. has been far less than many economists predicted. 有一些迹象表明，人工智能正在导致受其影响最大的行业的工资增长放缓，职位空缺减少，尤其对年轻求职者而言更是如此。此外，由于人工智能被用于撰写简历或筛选申请人，求职过程变得更加艰难，尤其是对初级职位的求职者而言。但总体而言，与人工智能直接相关的经济困境远小于许多经济学家的预测。 In China, the story is different. Its economic struggles, including high youth unemployment, consumer pullback on spending and a deflationary spiral, threaten to undercut Beijing’s vast investments in A.I. Chinese economists have recently issued warnings that the economy is vulnerable and potentially being made more precarious because of the country’s A.I.-centered allocation of spending. 在中国，情况则有所不同。其经济困境——包括青年高失业率、消费者削减开支和通货紧缩螺旋——有可能削弱北京在人工智能领域的巨额投资。中国经济学家最近发出警告称，经济本就脆弱，且可能因为以人工智能为中心的财政支出配置而变得更加岌岌可危。 周二，在北京举办的面向信息技术行业的展会中国国际信息通信展上，一款机器人成为焦点。 The nature of A.I. models in the U.S. and China are drastically different. 美中两国人工智能模型的性质截然不同。 In the United States, the leading artificial intelligence companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic, maintain tight control over how their technologies are used. They build elaborate guardrails, hoping to prevent users from spreading disinformation or hacking into computer networks. 在美国， OpenAI和Anthropic等领先人工智能公司对其技术的使用方式实施严格管控。它们建立了周密的防护机制，希望防止用户传播虚假信息或入侵计算机网络。 As concern mounts over the risks of A.I., these companies are calling for federal regulations that would toughen this approach. They say the government should review their A.I. technologies before release to ensure that the proper guardrails are in place — and many policymakers, lawmakers and pundits agree. 随着对人工智能风险担忧的加剧，这些公司呼吁制定联邦法规，以强化这种做法。他们表示，政府应在人工智能技术发布前进行审查查，以确保适当的防护措施到位——许多政策制定者、立法者和专家对此表示同意。 But the leading Chinese companies take a different stance. Companies like DeepSeek, Moonshot and Z.ai typically make their most powerful technologies “open source,” meaning anyone is free to use and modify these systems as they see fit. 但中国领先的公司采取不同的立场。像深度求索、月之暗面和智谱AI这样的公司通常将其最强大的技术“开源”，这意味着任何人都可以自由地根据需要使用和修改这些系统。 Open source has driven the development of computer software, the internet and artificial intelligence for decades. The idea is that technology advances faster when its computer code is freely available for anyone to examine, use and improve upon. 几十年来，开源一直推动着计算机软件、互联网和人工智能的发展。其理念是，当计算机代码可供任何人自由查阅、使用和改进时，技术进步会更快。 In open-sourcing their technologies, Chinese companies can essentially combine their resources and accelerate their efforts. And if U.S. regulators stifle the progress of American open-source projects — as some lawmakers are suggesting they should — China could gain a significant edge. 通过开源其技术，中国企业实际上可以整合其资源，加速研发进程。而且，如果美国监管机构扼杀美国开源项目的进展——正如一些立法者建议的那样——中国可能会获得重大优势。 If the best open-source systems come from China, many experts contend, developers across the globe will build atop Chinese technologies. This is already starting to happen, even in Silicon Valley. 许多专家认为，如果最好的开源系统来自中国，全球各地的开发者将基于中国技术进行开发。这种情况已经开始发生，甚至在硅谷也是如此。 “These models are still rough around the edges, but there are tasks where they are on par with the leading American systems,” said Rehaan Ahmad, a co-founder of the Silicon Valley start-up alphaXiv, who has used the latest Chinese technologies for the past several months. “这些模型在细节上仍显粗糙，但在某些任务上，它们与领先的美国系统不相上下，”硅谷初创公司alphaXiv的联合创始人雷汉·艾哈迈德说，他在过去几个月里一直在使用最新的中国技术。 Anyone can use these open-source technologies for malicious purposes, including, most notably, cyberattacks. But security experts say this is balanced by another phenomenon: Anyone can use the same technologies to defend against malicious attacks. 任何人都可以将这些开源技术用于恶意目的，其中最引人注目的是网络攻击。但安全专家表示，另一种现象抵消了这一风险：任何人都可以使用相同的技术来防御恶意攻击。 China could move ahead on electric power. 中国在电力领域可能取得领先。 Some believe that if China can build a viable chip industry, it could race ahead of the United States because of an advantage it has developed in another area: electrical power. 一些人认为，如果中国能建立起一个可行的芯片产业，它可能会超越美国，因为它在另一个领域发展了优势：电力。 Packed into giant data centers by the thousands, the leading chips require enormous amounts of electricity. They need so much electrical power, the big U.S. companies cannot get what they need from the existing power grid. Increasingly, they are turning to wind power or nuclear or even gas turbines installed alongside their data centers. 成千上万的领先芯片密集部署在巨型数据中心内，消耗着巨大的电能。它们需要的电力如此之多，以至于美国大公司无法从现有的电网中获得所需的一切。它们日益转向风能或核能，甚至在数据中心旁边安装燃气轮机。 “At a fundamental level, the tech industry is trying to convert electricity into intelligence,” said Mr. Feldman, the Cerebras chief executive. “It’s like a Dr. Seuss machine. In goes chips and power — and out comes intelligence.” “从根本上说，科技行业正试图将电力转化为智能，”Cerebras首席执行官费尔德曼说。“这就像一台苏斯博士笔下的机器。一边输入芯片和电力，另一边输出智能。” Although the United States has a significant edge in terms of chips, Mr. Feldman said, he believes that China could pull ahead because it has spent years rebuilding its electrical grid. “That is going to be a huge asset,” he said. “Our grid is 1950s technology.” 费尔德曼表示，尽管美国在芯片方面拥有显著优势，但他认为中国有可能后来居上，因为它花了数年时间重建电网。“这将是一笔巨大的资产，”他说。“我们的电网还是20世纪50年代的技术。” China leads in producing A.I. talent. 中国在培养人工智能人才方面处于领先地位。 As far back as 2024, studies showed that by some metrics, China had eclipsed the United States as the biggest producer of A.I. talent, generating almost half of the world’s leading researchers. By comparison, only about 18 percent came from the United States. 早在2024年，研究就表明，按照某些指标，中国已经超过美国，成为最大的人工智能人才出产国，培养了世界上近一半的领先研究人员。相比之下，只有约18%来自美国。 Researchers born and educated in China have for years played major roles inside leading U.S. artificial intelligence labs. And as newer studies have shown, they continue to drive important A.I. research across American industry and academia. But a growing number of them now stay in China, working for companies like Moonshot, Z.ai and DeepSeek. 出生在中国、并在中国接受教育的研究人员多年来一直在美国顶尖的人工智能实验室中发挥着重要作用。较新的研究表明，他们继续推动着整个美国工业界和学术界的重要人工智能研究。但如今，他们当中越来越多的人选择留在中国，为月之暗面、智谱AI和深度求索等公司工作。 Dustin Volz为时报撰写网络安全和情报方面的文章，他常驻华盛顿。 Cade Metz是时报记者，撰写有关人工智能、无人驾驶汽车、机器人、虚拟现实和其他新兴技术领域的报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

The rapidly shifting debate about the risks of A.I. has so consumed Silicon Valley, Washington and, in recent days, the United Nations that some observers have likened the U.S.-China summit to a Cold War tête-à-tête during the nuclear arms race. 但在最近几周，没有任何话题比双方能否 就人工智能的发展速度达成共识 更令全球关注。关于人工智能风险快速变化的辩论已彻底席卷硅谷和华盛顿，近日波及联合国，以至于一些观察家将此次美中峰会比作核军备竞赛期间的冷战一对一会谈。 Though some see the stakes this week as nothing short of civilizational , the expectations for any serious accord remain low. Even as China works to evade these controls, Chinese A.I. researchers often say that chip shortages are the biggest obstacle they face. 过去十年里，三届美国政府都 实施了出口管制 ，限制中国获取强大的芯片。尽管中国努力规避这些管制，但中国的人工智能研究人员经常表示，芯片短缺是他们面临的最大障碍。 The leading Chinese companies have spent hundreds of millions of dollars to secure the chips they need . The technology is also more embedded in day-to-day life, including service robots in hotels and restaurants, as well as medical chatbots at hospitals. 中国公民似乎普遍 对人工智能要乐观得多 ——事实上，根据毕马威去年对47个国家进行的一项 调查 ，他们是全世界对该技术抱有最大希望的人群之一。约69%的中国人表示，这项技术的好处大于风险，相比之下，持相同观点的美国人仅占35%。这项技术也更多地融入了日常生活，包括酒店和餐厅的服务机器人，以及医院的医疗聊天机器人。 The U.S. economy has so far been more resilient to huge investments in A.I. 到目前为止，美国经济在面对人工智能领域的巨额投资时表现出了更强的韧性。 Another advantage for the United States is that its economy has been more resilient during the A.I. boom. Stock indexes are near record highs, and worries of an A.I. bubble also have so far not materialized. Fears of job losses prompted by the technology proliferating throughout corporate America have yet to really appear in economic data. 美国的另一个优势是，在人工智能热潮期间，其经济更具韧性。股票指数接近历史高点，对人工智能泡沫的担忧迄今也未成为现实。尽管这项技术正在美国企业界广泛普及，但由此引发的失业担忧尚未在经济数据中真正显现。 There are some signs that A.I. is contributing to slower wage growth in jobs most exposed to the technology and fewer job openings, especially for young workers. And applying to jobs, especially for entry-level workers, has become even more daunting thanks to A.I. being used to either write résumés or screen applicants. But overall, the economic distress directly linked to A.I. has been far less than many economists predicted. 有一些迹象表明，人工智能正在导致受其影响最大的行业的 工资增长放缓 ，职位空缺减少，尤其对年轻求职者而言更是如此。此外，由于人工智能被用于撰写简历或筛选申请人，求职过程变得更加艰难，尤其是对初级职位的求职者而言。但总体而言，与人工智能直接相关的经济困境远小于许多经济学家的预测。 In China, the story is different . Its economic struggles, including high youth unemployment, consumer pullback on spending and a deflationary spiral, threaten to undercut Beijing’s vast investments in A.I. Chinese economists have recently issued warnings that the economy is vulnerable and potentially being made more precarious because of the country’s A.I.-centered allocation of spending. 在中国， 情况则有所不同 。其经济困境——包括青年高失业率、消费者削减开支和通货紧缩螺旋——有可能削弱北京在人工智能领域的巨额投资。中国经济学家最近发出警告称，经济本就脆弱，且可能因为以人工智能为中心的财政支出配置而变得更加岌岌可危。 周二，在北京举办的面向信息技术行业的展会中国国际信息通信展上，一款机器人成为焦点。 The nature of A.I. models in the U.S. and China are drastically different. 美中两国人工智能模型的性质截然不同。 In the United States, the leading artificial intelligence companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic, maintain tight control over how their technologies are used. They build elaborate guardrails, hoping to prevent users from spreading disinformation or hacking into computer networks . 在美国， OpenAI和Anthropic等领先人工智能公司对其技术的使用方式实施严格管控。它们建立了周密的防护机制，希望防止用户 传播虚假信息 或 入侵计算机网络 。 As concern mounts over the risks of A.I., these companies are calling for federal regulations that would toughen this approach. They say the government should review their A.I. technologies before release to ensure that the proper guardrails are in place — and many policymakers, lawmakers and pundits agree. 随着对人工智能风险担忧的加剧，这些公司呼吁制定联邦法规，以强化这种做法。他们表示，政府应在人工智能技术发布前进行审查查，以确保适当的防护措施到位——许多政策制定者、立法者和专家对此表示同意。 But the leading Chinese companies take a different stance. Companies like DeepSeek, Moonshot and Z.ai typically make their most powerful technologies “open source,” meaning anyone is free to use and modify these systems as they see fit. 但中国领先的公司采取不同的立场。像深度求索、月之暗面和智谱AI这样的公司通常将其最强大的技术“开源”，这意味着任何人都可以自由地根据需要使用和修改这些系统。 Open source has driven the development of computer software, the internet and artificial intelligence for decades. The idea is that technology advances faster when its computer code is freely available for anyone to examine, use and improve upon. 几十年来，开源一直推动着计算机软件、互联网和人工智能的发展。其理念是，当计算机代码可供任何人自由查阅、使用和改进时，技术进步会更快。 In open-sourcing their technologies, Chinese companies can essentially combine their resources and accelerate their efforts. And if U.S. regulators stifle the progress of American open-source projects — as some lawmakers are suggesting they should — China could gain a significant edge. 通过开源其技术，中国企业实际上可以整合其资源，加速研发进程。而且，如果美国监管机构扼杀美国开源项目的进展——正如一些立法者建议的那样——中国可能会获得重大优势。 If the best open-source systems come from China, many experts contend, developers across the globe will build atop Chinese technologies. This is already starting to happen, even in Silicon Valley . 许多专家认为，如果最好的开源系统来自中国，全球各地的开发者将基于中国技术进行开发。这种情况已经开始发生， 甚至在硅谷也是如此 。 “These models are still rough around the edges, but there are tasks where they are on par with the leading American systems,” said Rehaan Ahmad, a co-founder of the Silicon Valley start-up alphaXiv, who has used the latest Chinese technologies for the past several months. “这些模型在细节上仍显粗糙，但在某些任务上，它们与领先的美国系统不相上下，”硅谷初创公司alphaXiv的联合创始人雷汉·艾哈迈德说，他在过去几个月里一直在使用最新的中国技术。 Anyone can use these open-source technologies for malicious purposes, including, most notably, cyberattacks. But security experts say this is balanced by another phenomenon: Anyone can use the same technologies to defend against malicious attacks . 任何人都可以将这些开源技术用于恶意目的，其中最引人注目的是网络攻击。但安全专家表示，另一种现象抵消了这一风险：任何人都可以使用相同的技术来 防御恶意攻击 。 China could move ahead on electric power. 中国在电力领域可能取得领先。 Some believe that if China can build a viable chip industry, it could race ahead of the United States because of an advantage it has developed in another area: electrical power. 一些人认为，如果中国能建立起一个可行的芯片产业，它可能会超越美国，因为它在另一个领域发展了优势：电力。 Packed into giant data centers by the thousands, the leading chips require enormous amounts of electricity. They need so much electrical power, the big U.S. companies cannot get what they need from the existing power grid. Increasingly, they are turning to wind power or nuclear or even gas turbines installed alongside their data centers. 成千上万的领先芯片密集部署在巨型数据中心内，消耗着巨大的电能。它们需要的电力如此之多，以至于美国大公司无法从现有的电网中获得所需的一切。它们日益转向风能或核能，甚至在数据中心旁边安装燃气轮机。 “At a fundamental level, the tech industry is trying to convert electricity into intelligence,” said Mr. Feldman, the Cerebras chief executive. “It’s like a Dr. Seuss machine. In goes chips and power — and out comes intelligence.” “从根本上说，科技行业正试图将电力转化为智能，”Cerebras首席执行官费尔德曼说。“这就像一台苏斯博士笔下的机器。一边输入芯片和电力，另一边输出智能。” Although the United States has a significant edge in terms of chips, Mr. Feldman said, he believes that China could pull ahead because it has spent years rebuilding its electrical grid. “That is going to be a huge asset,” he said. “Our grid is 1950s technology.” 费尔德曼表示，尽管美国在芯片方面拥有显著优势，但他认为中国有可能后来居上，因为它花了数年时间重建电网。“这将是一笔巨大的资产，”他说。“我们的电网还是20世纪50年代的技术。” China leads in producing A.I. talent. 中国在培养人工智能人才方面处于领先地位。 As far back as 2024, studies showed that by some metrics, China had eclipsed the United States as the biggest producer of A.I. talent, generating almost half of the world’s leading researchers. By comparison, only about 18 percent came from the United States. 早在2024年， 研究就表明 ，按照某些指标，中国已经超过美国，成为最大的人工智能人才出产国，培养了世界上近一半的领先研究人员。相比之下，只有约18%来自美国。 Researchers born and educated in China have for years played major roles inside leading U.S. artificial intelligence labs. And as newer studies have shown, they continue to drive important A.I. research across American industry and academia. But a growing number of them now stay in China, working for companies like Moonshot, Z.ai and DeepSeek. 出生在中国、并在中国接受教育的研究人员多年来一直在美国顶尖的人工智能实验室中发挥着重要作用。较新的研究表明，他们继续 推动着整个美国工业界和学术界的重要人工智能研究 。但如今，他们当中越来越多的人选择留在中国，为月之暗面、智谱AI和深度求索等公司工作。 Dustin Volz 为时报撰写网络安全和情报方面的文章，他常驻华盛顿。 Cade Metz 是时报记者，撰写有关人工智能、无人驾驶汽车、机器人、虚拟现实和其他新兴技术领域的报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 中美关系正步入一个新时代
description: JESSICA CHEN WEISS2026年9月24日 Last year, the United States and China demonstrated they could inflict serious pain on each other. 去年，美中两国展示了给对方造成重创的能力。 The Trump administration imposed tariffs and technology controls; China hit back by restricting exports of rare earths and other materials essential for American industry. Factories and consumers on both sides of the Pacific felt the effects. But neither country could force the other to back down, and the confrontation ended last October, when they agreed to a yearlong truce. 特朗普政府加征关税并实施技术限制，中国则通过限制稀土及其他美国工业必需材料的出口予以反击。太平洋两岸的工厂和消费者均受到波及。但两国均未能迫使对方让步，这场对抗最终于去年10月以双方同意休战一年告终。 With that truce about to end, the meeting on Thursday between President Trump and President Xi Jinping of China opens a new chapter that could be pivotal for the relationship between the United States and China. 随着一年休战即将期满，特朗普总统与中国国家主席习近平周四举行的会晤开启了新篇章，这可能成为美中关系走向的关键节点。 The meeting at the White House is an opportunity for the two superpowers to embrace the undeniable lessons of the past year and begin building a durable détente by abandoning disruptive fantasies that either side can decisively “win.” 白宫的这场会晤为两个超级大国提供了契机：吸取过去一年不容回避的教训，摒弃任何一方能够取得决定性“胜利”的破坏性幻想，进而着手建立持久的缓和关系。 Beijing and Washington now know that neither can land a knockout blow because each possesses formidable advantages that the other struggles to match. 北京与华盛顿如今都已清楚，由于各自拥有对方难以企及的硬核优势，任何一方都无法给对方以致命一击。 America has unrivaled financial power and leads in semiconductor design, in making the equipment essential for chip manufacturing and in the most advanced artificial intelligence models. China is the world’s largest exporter. It dominates the global supply of rare-earth elements and critical minerals and the production of the high-powered magnets vital for advanced electronics, cars and weapons. Chinese-made chemicals and other ingredients are crucial for pharmaceuticals used in America. Regarding A.I., China has shot ahead in providing cheap open-weight models being rapidly adopted around the world, including in the United States. 美国拥有无可匹敌的金融实力，并在半导体设计、芯片制造核心设备以及最先进的人工智能模型方面保持领先。中国则是全球最大的出口国，主导着全球稀土元素与关键矿物的供应，以及先进电子产品、汽车和武器不可或缺的高性能磁体生产。中国制造的化学原料对在美国使用的药品至关重要。在人工智能领域，中国在提供廉价开放权重模型方面迅速走在前列，这些模型正在全球范围内被快速采用，包括在美国。 Building a lasting détente could prove as consequential for history as Cold War coexistence was for the United States and the Soviet Union. 建立持久的缓和关系的历史意义重大，可能堪比冷战时期和平共处对美苏关系的深远影响。 During the Cold War, the nuclear arms race and the prospect of mutually assured destruction caused Washington and Moscow to pull back from the brink. The same calculus holds today, but with an important difference: U.S.-Soviet trade was minimal, but the Chinese and American economies are deeply interdependent. 冷战期间，核军备竞赛与相互保证毁灭的前景促使华盛顿和莫斯科从悬崖边缘退缩。同样的逻辑在今天依然适用，但存在一个关键差异：美苏贸易当时微不足道，而如今中美两国经济高度相互依存。 Even after last year’s trade confrontation drove bilateral commerce down by 25 percent, China remained America’s third-largest trading partner after Mexico and Canada. Decoupling altogether is neither possible nor desirable, and attempts to weaponize one choke point invite sharp retaliation through another. What Washington and Beijing now face is an updated version of the Cold War’s deterrent: mutually assured economic disruption. 即使去年的贸易对抗导致双边贸易额下降了25%，中国依然是继墨西哥和加拿大之后美国的第三大贸易伙伴。完全脱钩既不现实也不可行，试图将某一“卡脖子”领域武器化则势必引发猛烈报复。华盛顿和北京如今面临的是冷战威慑机制的升级版本：相互保证经济破坏。 That is the logic of détente — the realization that continued escalation would be too costly. 这正是关系缓和的底层逻辑所在——双方意识到对抗持续升级的代价过于高昂。 The pursuit of decisive economic and strategic victory is futile, and it is not what the people bearing the costs of the resulting disruption want. Many Chinese and American citizens are tiring of confrontation. Young Americans, in particular, favor cooperation with China rather than confrontation, according to some surveys. In China, too, people are weary, increasingly opting out of the rat race rather than exhausting themselves in an economy that many see as geared toward national strength and the standoff with the United States rather than meeting their own needs. 追求决定性的经济和战略胜利是徒劳的，承担对抗代价的普通民众也不希望看到这种破坏。许多中美两国公民已对对抗感到厌倦。部分调查显示，美国年轻一代尤其倾向于对华合作而非对抗。在中国，民众同样感到疲累，越来越多的人选择退出内卷，不愿在一个被许多人视为服务于国家实力和中美对峙而非满足自身需求的经济环境中耗尽精力和心血。 Mr. Xi is looking ahead to next year’s Communist Party Congress — the gathering every five years that sets the party’s leadership and direction — and wants calm as it approaches that politically sensitive moment. With U.S. midterm elections looming, Mr. Trump is no doubt eager to secure agricultural trade deals with China that he can present as wins for U.S. farmers. Thursday’s meeting may yield only modest gestures, but the encounter offers something more important over the long run: a chance for both governments to reaffirm what the past year has made clear. 习近平正着眼于明年的中国共产党全国代表大会，希望在这一政治敏感时期临近之际保持平稳局势。这一每五年举行一次的大会将确定党的领导层和发展方向。而随着美国中期选举临近，特朗普无疑渴望与中国达成农产品贸易协议，以便将其包装成一场美国农民的胜利。周四的会晤或许只会达成一些适度举措，但从长远来看，这次会晤提供了更具深远意义的契机：让两国政府重申过去一年所明确的事实。 Artificial intelligence is expected to be a major topic, and perhaps no issue better illustrates the dangers both countries now face. The warning signs are mounting. In the United States, A.I. systems have tapped into sensitive networks and otherwise behaved unpredictably. And after a California security firm revealed this month that A.I. had helped it find a way to hijack accounts on WeChat, the dominant Chinese messaging app, China’s top spy chief warned that A.I. could slip beyond control and threaten political and social stability. 人工智能预计将成为主要议题，也许没有哪个问题能比它更好地凸显两国当前面临的风险。警示信号正不断增加。在美国，人工智能系统已侵入敏感网络并展现出其他不可预测的行为。本月，加州一家安全公司披露人工智能帮助其找到了劫持中国主导社交应用微信账号的方法，中国最高情报主管随后发出警告，称人工智能可能会失控并威胁政治与社会稳定。 Such concerns make it all the more important for China and the United States to lower the temperature and keep communication channels open. They could start with discussions that focus initially on common enemies such as ransomware gangs that could use A.I. to exploit vulnerabilities in software, networks and critical industries. 这些担忧使得中美两国降低对抗热度、保持沟通渠道畅通显得尤为重要。双方可以从聚焦共同敌人的讨论切入，例如可能利用人工智能攻击软件、网络和关键工业漏洞的勒索软件团伙。 None of this means this week’s meeting will produce a major breakthrough, or that some grand geopolitical bargain is on the horizon, or that the two nations will stop jostling over trade, technology and global influence. 这并不意味着本周的会晤会取得重大突破，也不意味着某种宏大的地缘政治妥协即将来临，或是两国将停止在贸易、技术和全球影响力方面的角逐。 What truly matters is that both absorb the reality that maximalist demands and threats serve neither country’s interests and begin laying the foundations for a more stable future. Washington must understand that China seeks greater influence in the world and less vulnerability to foreign pressure, not to cripple one of its biggest trading partners. Beijing, for its part, must recognize that every time it weaponizes its dominance of critical metals, it hastens U.S. efforts to diversify its own supply chains, thereby eroding China’s leverage and hardening American fears about Beijing’s intentions. 真正重要的是，双方都能认清极限施压和威胁不符合任何一方利益这一现实，并开始为更稳定的未来奠定基础。华盛顿必须明白，中国寻求提升国际影响力和抵御外部压力的能力，并非为了击垮其最大的贸易伙伴之一；北京方面也必须意识到，每当其将关键金属主导地位武器化时，都会加速美国推进供应链多元化的努力，从而削弱中国的筹码，并加剧美国对北京意图的担忧。 The larger promise of embracing a durable détente lies not only in avoiding disruption now, but in widening what may become possible. A more stable relationship could create regular communication, make crises easier to manage and open space for sustained and badly needed work on humanity’s biggest challenges, such as A.I., climate change and global health, which neither country can solve alone. 建立持久缓和关系的更大意义不仅在于避免当下的破坏，还在于拓展未来的可能性。更加稳定的关系能够建立定期沟通机制，使危机更容易管控，并为在人类面临的最大挑战（如人工智能、气候变化和全球卫生等任何一国都无法单独解决的问题）上开展持续且急需的合作开辟空间。 This doesn’t require mutual trust, only the wisdom and restraint to keep competition from consuming the rest of the relationship. 这并不需要相互信任，只需要保持理性与克制，避免竞争吞噬两国关系的其余部分。 Jessica Chen Weiss是约翰·霍普金斯大学高级国际研究学院美国、中国与全球事务未来研究所所长。她即将出版《中国想要什么：以及这对世界意味着什么》一书。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

Regarding A.I., China has shot ahead in providing cheap open-weight models being rapidly adopted around the world, including in the United States . 美国拥有无可匹敌的金融实力，并在半导体设计、芯片制造核心设备以及最先进的人工智能模型方面保持领先。中国则是全球最大的 出口国 ，主导着全球稀土元素与关键矿物的供应，以及先进电子产品、汽车和武器不可或缺的高性能磁体生产。中国制造的化学原料对在美国使用的药品至关重要。在人工智能领域，中国在提供廉价开放权重模型方面迅速走在前列，这些模型正在全球范围内被快速采用，包括 在美国 。 Building a lasting détente could prove as consequential for history as Cold War coexistence was for the United States and the Soviet Union. 建立持久的缓和关系的历史意义重大，可能堪比冷战时期和平共处对美苏关系的深远影响。 During the Cold War, the nuclear arms race and the prospect of mutually assured destruction caused Washington and Moscow to pull back from the brink. The same calculus holds today, but with an important difference: U.S.-Soviet trade was minimal, but the Chinese and American economies are deeply interdependent. 冷战期间，核军备竞赛与相互保证毁灭的前景促使华盛顿和莫斯科从悬崖边缘退缩。同样的逻辑在今天依然适用，但存在一个关键差异：美苏贸易当时微不足道，而如今中美两国经济高度相互依存。 Even after last year’s trade confrontation drove bilateral commerce down by 25 percent , China remained America’s third-largest trading partner after Mexico and Canada. Decoupling altogether is neither possible nor desirable, and attempts to weaponize one choke point invite sharp retaliation through another. What Washington and Beijing now face is an updated version of the Cold War’s deterrent: mutually assured economic disruption. 即使去年的贸易对抗导致双边贸易额 下降了25% ，中国依然是继墨西哥和加拿大之后美国的 第三大 贸易伙伴。完全脱钩既不现实也不可行，试图将某一“卡脖子”领域武器化则势必引发猛烈报复。华盛顿和北京如今面临的是冷战威慑机制的升级版本：相互保证经济破坏。 That is the logic of détente — the realization that continued escalation would be too costly. 这正是关系缓和的底层逻辑所在——双方意识到对抗持续升级的代价过于高昂。 The pursuit of decisive economic and strategic victory is futile, and it is not what the people bearing the costs of the resulting disruption want. Many Chinese and American citizens are tiring of confrontation. Young Americans, in particular, favor cooperation with China rather than confrontation, according to some surveys. In China, too, people are weary, increasingly opting out of the rat race rather than exhausting themselves in an economy that many see as geared toward national strength and the standoff with the United States rather than meeting their own needs . 追求决定性的经济和战略胜利是徒劳的，承担对抗代价的普通民众也不希望看到这种破坏。许多中美两国公民已对对抗感到厌倦。部分调查显示，美国年轻一代尤其 倾向于对华合作 而非对抗。在中国，民众同样感到疲累，越来越多的人选择 退出内卷 ，不愿在一个被许多人视为服务于国家实力和中美对峙 而非满足自身需求 的经济环境中耗尽精力和心血。 Mr. Xi is looking ahead to next year’s Communist Party Congress — the gathering every five years that sets the party’s leadership and direction — and wants calm as it approaches that politically sensitive moment. With U.S. midterm elections looming, Mr. Trump is no doubt eager to secure agricultural trade deals with China that he can present as wins for U.S. farmers. Thursday’s meeting may yield only modest gestures, but the encounter offers something more important over the long run: a chance for both governments to reaffirm what the past year has made clear. 习近平正着眼于明年的中国共产党全国代表大会，希望在这一政治敏感时期临近之际保持平稳局势。这一每五年举行一次的大会将确定党的领导层和发展方向。而随着美国中期选举临近，特朗普无疑渴望与中国达成农产品贸易协议，以便将其包装成一场美国农民的胜利。周四的会晤或许只会达成一些适度举措，但从长远来看，这次会晤提供了更具深远意义的契机：让两国政府重申过去一年所明确的事实。 Artificial intelligence is expected to be a major topic, and perhaps no issue better illustrates the dangers both countries now face. The warning signs are mounting. In the United States, A.I. systems have tapped into sensitive networks and otherwise behaved unpredictably . And after a California security firm revealed this month that A.I. had helped it find a way to hijack accounts on WeChat, the dominant Chinese messaging app, China’s top spy chief warned that A.I. could slip beyond control and threaten political and social stability. 人工智能预计将成为主要议题，也许没有哪个问题能比它更好地凸显两国当前面临的风险。警示信号正不断增加。在美国，人工智能系统已 侵入 敏感网络并展现出其他 不可预测的行为 。本月，加州一家安全公司 披露 人工智能帮助其找到了劫持中国主导社交应用微信账号的方法，中国最高情报主管随后 发出警告 ，称人工智能可能会失控并威胁政治与社会稳定。 Such concerns make it all the more important for China and the United States to lower the temperature and keep communication channels open. They could start with discussions that focus initially on common enemies such as ransomware gangs that could use A.I. to exploit vulnerabilities in software, networks and critical industries. 这些担忧使得中美两国降低对抗热度、保持沟通渠道畅通显得尤为重要。双方可以从聚焦共同敌人的 讨论 切入，例如可能利用人工智能攻击软件、网络和关键工业漏洞的勒索软件团伙。 None of this means this week’s meeting will produce a major breakthrough, or that some grand geopolitical bargain is on the horizon, or that the two nations will stop jostling over trade, technology and global influence. 这并不意味着本周的会晤会取得重大突破，也不意味着某种宏大的地缘政治妥协即将来临，或是两国将停止在贸易、技术和全球影响力方面的角逐。 What truly matters is that both absorb the reality that maximalist demands and threats serve neither country’s interests and begin laying the foundations for a more stable future. Washington must understand that China seeks greater influence in the world and less vulnerability to foreign pressure, not to cripple one of its biggest trading partners. Beijing, for its part, must recognize that every time it weaponizes its dominance of critical metals, it hastens U.S. efforts to diversify its own supply chains, thereby eroding China’s leverage and hardening American fears about Beijing’s intentions. 真正重要的是，双方都能认清极限施压和威胁不符合任何一方利益这一现实，并开始为更稳定的未来奠定基础。华盛顿必须明白，中国寻求提升国际影响力和抵御外部压力的能力，并非为了击垮其最大的贸易伙伴之一；北京方面也必须意识到，每当其将关键金属主导地位武器化时，都会加速美国推进供应链多元化的努力，从而削弱中国的筹码，并加剧美国对北京意图的担忧。 The larger promise of embracing a durable détente lies not only in avoiding disruption now, but in widening what may become possible. A more stable relationship could create regular communication, make crises easier to manage and open space for sustained and badly needed work on humanity’s biggest challenges, such as A.I., climate change and global health, which neither country can solve alone. 建立持久缓和关系的更大意义不仅在于避免当下的破坏，还在于拓展未来的可能性。更加稳定的关系能够建立定期沟通机制，使危机更容易管控，并为在人类面临的最大挑战（如人工智能、气候变化和全球卫生等任何一国都无法单独解决的问题）上开展持续且急需的合作开辟空间。 This doesn’t require mutual trust, only the wisdom and restraint to keep competition from consuming the rest of the relationship. 这并不需要相互信任，只需要保持理性与克制，避免竞争吞噬两国关系的其余部分。 Jessica Chen Weiss是约翰·霍普金斯大学高级国际研究学院美国、中国与全球事务未来研究所所长。她即将出版《中国想要什么：以及这对世界意味着什么》一书。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 美国人对华态度回暖，更多人以积极眼光看待中国
description: ANTON TROIANOVSKI2026年9月24日 Source: Pew Research Center. President Trump’s shift to a friendlier stance on China mirrors a startling change in public opinion. Across the political spectrum, more Americans are seeing China in a positive light. 特朗普总统转向更友好的对华立场，折射出公众舆论中令人惊讶的变化。无论政治立场如何，越来越多的美国人正以积极眼光看待中国。 Surveys from leading pollsters, including two released this week, show that China’s image in the United States has improved markedly in recent years. People are still skeptical about China, but as Mr. Trump prepares to give the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, a warm welcome in Washington this week, his accommodation echoes what some experts see as a desire among Americans for a more stable relationship with Beijing. 包括本周发布的两份报告在内，来自主流民调机构的调查显示，近年来中国在美国的形象显著改善。人们对中国仍存疑虑，但随着特朗普准备本周在华盛顿热烈欢迎中国领导人习近平，他的顺应态度印证了部分专家的观点，即美国人渴望与北京建立更稳定的关系。 “There really is this warming toward China, even if on balance views still remain fairly negative,” said Laura Silver, an associate director at the Pew Research Center, which published survey data on Wednesday showing that 54 percent of Americans now have a “cold” view of China, compared with 68 percent in 2021. “对华态度确实在回暖，即使总体看法依然相当负面，”皮尤研究中心副主任劳拉·西尔弗(Laura Silver)说。该中心于周三发布的调查数据显示，目前有54%的美国人对中国持“冷淡”看法，而2021年该比例为68%。 The surveys do not pinpoint the reasons for the shift, which appears to be more pronounced among younger Americans. But experts point to fading memories of the coronavirus pandemic, awareness of China’s tech innovations and disaffection with Mr. Trump’s trade wars as contributing to a changing mood that could affect how U.S. politicians approach China. 这些调查并未阐明情绪转变的具体原因，且这种转变在年轻美国人中似乎相对显著。但专家指出，对新冠大流行的记忆淡化，对中国科技创新的认知，以及对特朗普贸易战的不满共同促成了一种可能影响美国政客对华态度的情绪转变。 The Chicago Council on Global Affairs, a think tank that has long studied the country’s foreign policy views, has picked up a reversal over just the last two years. By 2024, the share of Americans who favored “friendly cooperation and engagement with China” had declined to just 40 percent. But when the organization asked the question again this July, that number had risen to 57 percent, including 68 percent of Democrats and 43 percent of Republicans, according to data published this week. 长期研究美国外交政策观点的智库芝加哥全球事务委员会发现，仅在过去两年里就发生了一次态度逆转。2024年，支持“与中国进行友好合作与接触”的美国人比例一度降至仅40%。然而，根据本周公布的数据，当该组织今年7月再次调查此问题时，这一比例已升至57%，其中包括68%的民主党人和43%的共和党人。 “The attitudes toward China have been really surprising,” said Dina Smeltz, a former State Department official who oversees the Chicago Council’s polling. “They’ve shifted from a majority wanting to limit the rise of China and limit its influence to now a majority of Americans wanting to engage cooperatively with China.” “民众对中国的态度着实令人惊讶，”负责监督芝加哥委员会民调的前国务院官员迪娜·斯梅尔茨说。“他们已从多数人希望限制中国的崛起与影响力，转变为如今多数美国人希望与中国合作接触。” The research organization Gallup found earlier this year that the share of Americans with a favorable view of China had risen to 34 percent, more than double the low point in 2023. 研究机构盖洛普今年早些时候发现，对中国持好感的美国人比例已升至34%，是2023年低谷时期的两倍多。 The surveys all point to a changed national mood compared with a decade ago, when Mr. Trump’s harsh anti-China rhetoric helped define his winning presidential campaign. President Joseph R. Biden Jr. largely maintained and expanded Mr. Trump’s tough policies, including tariffs and export controls, cementing what appeared to be a bipartisan consensus that the United States needed to push back hard against China’s rise. 这些调查均反映出与十年前截然不同的国民情绪，当时特朗普严厉的反华言论助推了他的胜选。小约瑟夫·R·拜登总统在很大程度上维持并扩大了特朗普的强硬政策，包括关税和出口管制，巩固了一个似乎是两党共识的观念：美国需要强硬反击中国的崛起。 Now that consensus has weakened, as made plain by Mr. Trump himself. He stepped back last year from tariffs as high as 145 percent to pursue what has looked like an effort of reconciliation with China. It was on display in his deferential visit to Beijing in April and what is expected to be a lavish welcome for Mr. Xi this week — all without Beijing making major concessions on longstanding U.S. demands on trade or security issues. 正如特朗普本人所表明的那样，现在这种共识已经弱化。去年，他从高达145%的关税政策上退让，似乎在寻求对华和解。这体现在他4月访问北京时的恭顺，以及预计本周对习近平的隆重欢迎中——而这一切都是在北京没有就贸易或安全等美国长期诉求做出重大让步的情况下发生的。 人们在拍摄特朗普总统5月访问北京时的车队。 The polls show that Republicans remain more hawkish on China than Democrats, though Republicans’ views of China have grown more positive as well — perhaps a reflection of Mr. Trump’s own shift. Despite the country’s polarization, Democrats have also moved in the same direction. 民调表明，共和党人在对华问题上仍比民主党人更为鹰派，不过共和党人对中国的看法也变得更加正面——这或许反映了特朗普自身的立场转变。尽管美国存在政治极化，但民主党人也正朝着相同方向发展。 Just a year or two ago, politicians could “propose almost any kind of tough policy against China and the public would be behind it,” said Bruce Stokes, an expert on foreign policy polling at the German Marshall Fund, a think tank. “This public opinion data seems to suggest that support for a tough-on-China policy has weakened a little bit.” 仅仅一两年前，政客们“提出几乎任何针对中国的强硬政策，公众都会予以支持”，智库德国马歇尔基金会外交政策民调专家布鲁斯·斯托克斯说。“这些民调数据似乎表明，对强硬对华政策的支持已略有减弱。” Americans’ views of China, of course, could quickly shift again, especially amid fears of its artificial intelligence prowess and the risk of armed conflict over Taiwan. Pollsters note that Americans generally spend little time thinking about foreign policy and rarely let international issues determine how they vote. 当然，美国人对中国的看法可能会再次迅速转变，特别是在对其人工智能实力的担忧以及因台湾问题引发武装冲突风险的背景下。民调专家指出，美国人通常很少花时间思考外交政策，也极少让国际问题决定其投票意向。 But people who study the U.S. relationship with China see the polling figures as reflective of a changing geopolitical dynamic and, perhaps, angst over the United States’ place in the world. In the Pew and Chicago Council polls, younger adults are significantly more positively disposed toward China, evidence of a generational shift. 但研究美中关系的人士认为，民调数据反映出不断变化的地缘政治动态，或许也折射出对美国国际地位的焦虑。在皮尤和芝加哥委员会的民调中，较年轻成年人对中国的态度明显更加积极，这印证了代际转变。 “Younger people have known China as a superpower,” Ms. Silver, the Pew researcher, said. Older generations, by contrast, are more likely to associate China with the developing world, Communism and the Tiananmen Square massacre of 1989, she said. “年轻人所认识的中国是一个超级大国，”皮尤研究员西尔弗说。她表示，相比之下，老一代人更有可能将中国与发展中国家、共产主义以及1989年的天安门广场大屠杀联系起来。 Younger people may also be more aware of China’s technological innovations and cultural exports, as evidenced by the “Chinamaxxing” trends ricocheting around the internet. That awareness comes in contrast to a sense of a decline in the United States’ global standing: 62 percent of Americans say the country is respected less in the world today than it was 10 years ago, according to the Chicago Council. 年轻群体可能也对中国的技术创新和文化输出有更多认知，在互联网上风靡的“中国最大化(Chinamaxxing)”趋势便是明证。这种认知与对美国全球地位衰退的感受形成反差：根据芝加哥委员会的数据，62%的美国人认为，当今美国在世界上受到的尊重不如10年前。 “You see fears of what’s happening to America be refracted through assessments of China,” said Nick Zeller, a scholar at the Carter Center in Atlanta who tracks how China and the United States perceive each other. “This positive assessment toward China has more to do with American political tumult domestically than it does China itself.” “你会发现，对美国现状的恐惧通过对中国的评估折射出来，”位于亚特兰大的卡特中心追踪中美互视视角的学者尼克·泽勒表示。“这种对中国的正面评估更多地与美国国内的政治动荡有关，而非中国本身。” Anton Troianovski自华盛顿为《纽约时报》报道有关美国外交政策和国家安全的文章。他此前曾在莫斯科和柏林任驻外记者。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
